battle.name: 韓相國起義
battle.theater: 河南梁郡宋城至襄城一線
battle.brief: 大業九年七月，楊玄感圍東都洛陽，梁郡宋城平民韓相國舉兵響應，被推為河南道元帥，旬月之間聚眾十餘萬，攻剽郡縣，轉戰至襄城。隋廷主力壓在遼東前線，東都只剩重甲精兵與騎兵守城。卡面的羅馬重步兵並未出現在東亞，它對應的正是本役兩套裝備體系：隋軍鎧仗齊備，起義軍卻是執單刀柳楯、無弓矢甲冑。

kit.name: 羅馬重步兵
kit.history: 分段鎧甲配重盾。羅馬的戰力靠的是補充兵源與補給線，不是靠重裝。

countries: 韓相國起義爆發於隋大業九年（613年）河南道，交戰雙方是隋朝官軍與梁郡宋城起義眾。隋廷方面，煬帝坐鎮涿郡，經營遼東第二次征高句麗，京師宿衛與關右兵力大半被抽調到北方；洛陽東都一線由留守樊子蓋主持，他以刑峻聞名，屬下稍有違令即斬以徇。東都守備分散在數支部隊：河南令達奚善意率精兵五千，屯漢王寺拒敵；作監裴弘策將八千人屯白司馬板；代王侗所遣刑部尚書衛文升率步騎四萬，自華陰鼓行出崤、澠，直趨城北，屯金谷，後移屯邙山之陽；左候衛將軍屈突通屯河陽，濟河軍於破陵，截斷西路援軍；左翊衛大將軍宇文述與虎賁郎將陳稜奉詔討逆；右驍衛大將軍來護兒放棄遼東戰事，率舟師自東萊回援；虎威將軍王世充亦在討逆序列之中。起義方面，韓相國是梁郡宋城縣的平民，楊玄感圍東都之際起兵響應，被玄感任命為河南道元帥。他的十餘萬眾由鄉里部曲臨時徵集而成，無固定編制與後方營區，數量上遠勝官軍在地的一支偏師，組織與補給則完全依靠攻剽郡縣就地取給。同一時間，河南、山東、江淮、南越的起義互相呼應，餘杭劉元進、吳郡朱燮與晉陵管崇、孟海公、格謙、白瑜娑、韓進洛與甄寶車、郝孝德等先後舉兵，使隋廷無法集中兵力逐次平定。
countriesEn: Han Xianguo's rising broke out in Henan Dao in the ninth year of the Daye era (613). The two sides were the regular army of the Sui dynasty and the rebel bands mustered in Songcheng by Han Xianguo, a commoner of Liang Commandery. On the Sui side Emperor Yang sat at Zhuojun, running the second Goguryeo campaign in Liaodong, and most of the capital's household guard and the Guanzhong levies had been drawn away to the north. The Eastern Capital at Luoyang was administered by the garrison commander Fan Zigan, who was known for severity: a single order broken was enough for a man to be beheaded in front of the ranks. The capital's defence was split among several columns. The magistrate of Henan, Da Xie Shanyi, led five thousand picked troops and entrenched at Hanyang Temple. The Director of Works, Pei Hongce, took eight thousand men to post at the White Sima Ford. Wei Wensheng, Minister of Justice, was sent by the Prince of Dai with twenty thousand foot and horse; he marched out of Mount Xiao and Mount Mian, drove straight for the city from the north, camped first at Jingu and later on the sunny side of Mangshan. Qu Tutong, Left Commandant of the Guards, camped at Heyang, forded the river and drew up at Poling to seal the western approach. Yuwen Shu, Left General of the Left Flank Guard, and Chen Ling, Colonel of the Household Guard, received imperial orders to put down the revolt. Lai Hu'er, Right General of the Valiant Guards, abandoned his eastern naval operations and came back from Donglai with his fleet, and Wang Shichong, General of the Fierce Guard, also appears in the columns sent against the rebels. On the rebel side Han Xianguo was a commoner of Songcheng County in Liang Commandery. He rose when Yang Xuangan besieged the Eastern Capital, and Xuangan appointed him commander-in-chief of Henan Dao. His host of more than a hundred thousand was hastily summoned from village levies; it had no regular establishment and no rear area. In numbers it far exceeded the regular detachments available locally, yet its organisation and its supplies rested entirely on seizing the county seats. At the same moment revolts in Henan, Shandong, Jianghuai and Lingnan answered one another: Liu Yuanjin at Yuhang, Zhu Xie and Guan Chong in Wu and Jinling, Meng Haigong, Ge Qian, Bai Yusha, Han Jinluo together with Zhen Baoche, and Hao Xiaode all rose in the same year, so the Sui court could never concentrate its troops to defeat them one at a time.
people: 韓相國本人是這場起義唯一留下姓名的首領，史籍只作「梁郡民韓相國」，鄉里不詳，相國二字是起義眾給他的尊稱而非正式官爵。他生於六世紀，至大業九年舉兵，除姓氏與「相國」之號外無一字可考，可確定的只有這條時間線：楊玄感圍東都時起兵響應，被授河南道元帥，旬月聚眾十餘萬，攻剽郡縣，轉戰至襄城，最後被隋吏擒獲，傳首東都。推動他起兵的楊玄感是禮部尚書，出身關西勛戚，兄弟分任虎賁郎將與鷹揚郎將；他在黎陽督運漕糧時逗遛漕運、假稱水路多盜，令渡遼諸軍乏食，又密遣家奴偽作使者詐稱來護兒已反，隨後以討來護兒為名，於六月乙巳閉黎陽城，大索男夫，取帆布為牟甲，署官屬皆准開皇之舊，移書傍郡令各縣發兵會於倉所。他每戰身先士卒，所向摧陷，眾至十萬，兵敗於董杜原後與弟積善徒步至葭蘆戍，謂積善曰「我不能受人戮辱」，令其殺己。真正決定東都攻防節奏的是李密，薄山公，玄感之謀主：他獻上策直搗幽州臨渝、次策西取長安、下策襲取東都，玄感選了下策；密又屢勸他不可急於稱尊號，密私下對所親說「楚公好反而不欲勝，吾屬今為虜矣」。東都方面的關鍵人物還有樊子蓋，他斬裴弘策以肅軍令，使將吏震肅、無人敢仰視；衛文升為示士卒以必死，發兵時掘楊素之塚、焚其骸骨；屈突通、宇文述、來護兒、王世充各路兵馬在河陽、破陵、弘農一線完成合擊。事後御史大夫裴蘊、大理卿鄭善果、刑部侍郎骨儀奉命推究玄感黨與。
peopleEn: Han Xianguo himself is the only leader of this rising whose name is recorded. History calls him nothing but 'the commoner of Liang Commandery, Han Xianguo'. His home village is unknown, and the two characters 'xiangguo' are a title the rebels gave him rather than a regular office. He was born in the sixth century and rose in arms in the ninth year of Daye. Apart from his surname and that honorary title not a single character of his record survives; what can be fixed is only the sequence. When Yang Xuangan besieged the Eastern Capital he rose in answer, was made commander-in-chief of Henan Dao, drew more than a hundred thousand men within a few tens of days, raided the county seats, fought his way through to Xiangcheng, and was finally taken by Sui officials and his head sent to the Eastern Capital. The man who set him moving was Yang Xuangan, Minister of Rites, born into a powerful clan of western exiles whose brothers held the rank of Colonel of the Household Guard and Eagle-Raising Colonel. While supervising the transport of grain at Liyang he held up the river convoys, claiming that pirates on the water made it unsafe to sail, so that the armies crossing into Liaodong went short of food; he also sent a family servant disguised as an envoy to spread the false report that Lai Hu'er had rebelled. Then, under the pretext of marching against Lai Hu'er, he shut the gates of Liyang on the yi-si day of the sixth month, seized all the men of the town, took sailcloth for a felt cap and armour, and set up officials as they had been in the Kaihuang era. He led in person at every action, broke the enemy wherever he went, and his host grew to a hundred thousand. After the defeat at Dongdu he walked with his younger brother Jishan to Jialu Garrison and told Jishan, 'I cannot bear to be taken and put to death; you had better kill me.' The man who really shaped the course of the siege was Li Mi, Lord of Boshan, who served as Xuangan's adviser. He proposed three plans: strike at Youzhou and hold the passes of Linyu; march west and seize Chang'an; or fall on the Eastern Capital. Xuangan chose the third. Mi also warned him repeatedly against proclaiming a new title too early, and said privately to his own people, 'Duke Chu loves to rebel but does not want to win; we are done for.' On the Sui side Fan Zigan, the garrison commander, executed Pei Hongce to enforce discipline, after which the officers and men were so subdued that no one dared lift his head. Wei Wensheng, to show his troops they must expect to die, opened the tomb of Yang Su and burned his bones before the army marched. Qu Tutong, Yuwen Shu, Lai Hu'er and Wang Shichong closed in along the line of Heyang, Poling and Hongnong. Afterwards the Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun, the Minister of Justice Zheng Shanguo and the Vice Minister of Justice Gu Yi were ordered to sift out the followers of Xuangan.
kits: 卡面這件羅馬重步兵，拉丁名 legionarius，屬公元前二世紀末至帝國早期的重裝步兵，配分段鎧甲與重盾，它的價值不在甲冑本身，而在背後那套補充兵源與補給線的體系。這套東西在隋末的東亞戰場上並不存在，但同一場戰爭裡正有兩套可對照的裝備。隋軍一方是標準的重裝步兵對手：東都守軍出動時鎧仗齊備，裴弘策部八千人在白司馬板連敗之後「棄鎧仗者太半」，達奚善意五千精兵、衛文升步騎二萬配明光鎧與兜鍪，長槊、環首刀與弓箭並用，另有臂弓與蹶張弩作遠程火力；攻城方向則有堆積如丘山的軍資器械與攻具，遼東前線曾造布囊百餘萬口盛土築魚梁大道，又作八輪樓車高出城牆俯射城內。起義軍一方完全相反：楊玄感所部「其兵皆執單刀柳楯，無弓矢甲冑」，韓相國的十餘萬眾屬同類鄉里部曲，執單刀、柳木盾、竹木槊與柴刀，弓矢與甲冑極缺，坐騎有限，糧食全靠攻剽郡縣與就地徵集，連營帳器具都是臨時拋棄物。與卡面同源的還有結構：羅馬重步兵靠不斷補充的徵召兵與糧秣維持，隋廷靠漕運與府兵、募兵維持，韓相國卻只有十餘萬人的數量而沒有後方。起義軍的裝備結構說明，這場戰爭裡真正決定勝負的從來不是重裝，而是有沒有補給線與能不能及時補充。
kitsEn: The card shows a Roman heavy infantryman, legionarius in Latin, a heavy infantryman of the late second century BC and the early Empire, equipped with segmented armour and a heavy shield. Its value lay not in the armour itself but in the system of replacement troops and supply behind it. That system never existed on an East Asian battlefield in the late Sui, yet this very war contains two equipment systems that can be laid against it. The Sui troops are the standard heavy-infantry opponent: the capital's garrison went into action fully accoutred, and after the repeated defeats at the White Sima Ford Pei Hongce's eight thousand men 'abandoned their armour and weapons to the number of more than half'; Da Xie Shanyi's five thousand picked men and Wei Wensheng's twenty thousand foot and horse were equipped with bright armour and helmets, using long spears, ring-pommel sabres and bows together, with arm bows and strong-pull crossbows for longer range. For the attack they had a stock of military stores, weapons and siege equipment piled as high as a hill: at the Liaodong front they made more than a million cloth sacks full of earth to raise a fish-beam causeway, and built eight-wheeled tower carts that stood above the wall and shot down into the city. The rebel side is the exact opposite. Xuangan's men 'all carried a single-edged sabre and a willow shield, without bows and arrows, without armour or helmet', and the hundred thousand odd men of Han Xianguo were the same kind of village levy, with single-edged sabres, willow-wood shields, bamboo and wooden spears and billhooks, very few bows and no armour at all, few mounts, and food obtained only by raiding the county seats and taking what was locally available; even the gear of the camp was thrown away as they moved. The structure is the same as on the card: the Roman heavy infantryman was sustained by continually replaced conscripts and grain, the Sui court by river transport together with military colonies and recruited men, whereas Han Xianguo had nothing but the bare number of a hundred thousand men and no rear area. The equipment of the rebels shows that what decided this war was never the weight of armour, but the presence of a supply line and the ability to replace losses in time.
tactics: 起義軍採取的是流動性的徵發與掠地戰術。韓相國在楊玄感兵鋒指向洛陽時於梁郡響應，先聚眾，後四出攻剽郡縣，靠郡縣守軍空虛與官吏反應遲緩取給人數與物資，再向襄城方向轉移，尋求與玄感主力呼應。消息傳播極快，玄感在董杜原敗亡的消息先一步抵達，起義眾隨即鬆散。隋軍的部署則有層次：達奚善意以精兵五千據漢王寺，迎戰自偃師南緣洛水西入的楊積善；裴弘策將八千人列陣白司馬板，迎擊自白司馬板逾邙山南入的楊玄挺，一日之內五戰，屢退屢收散兵結陣再鬥；衛文升自華陰出崤、澠，且戰且行直趨城北，屯金谷再屯邙山之陽，與玄感一日十餘合地糾纏，靠消耗與接戰節奏拖住對手，直到楊玄挺中流矢死，玄感軍才略退。援軍方面，屈突通先屯河陽，待樊子蓋數擊其營、分兵之隙才濟河軍於破陵，玄感被迫分為西抗文升、東拒通兩軍；來護兒自東萊放棄海路戰役回師，宇文述等自涿郡乘傳追進。玄感最後放棄東都圍城，詐稱已破東都取關西，西趣潼關，至皇天原布陳亙五十里且戰且行，一日三敗，終於董杜原崩潰，往葭蘆戍方向步行突圍。攻城技術上，隋廷在遼東備妥魚梁大道與八輪樓車，卻在夜半二更全部棄置率軍回救，這是整場戰役最關鍵的戰略轉折：東都守軍得到生力軍，起義軍失去時間。
tacticsEn: The rebels used a mobile tactic of hasty mustering and raiding. When Yang Xuangan's spearhead turned towards Luoyang, Han Xianguo answered in Liang Commandery: first he gathered a host, then he sent them out in all directions to raid the county seats, taking both men and supplies from a province whose county garrisons were hollow and whose officials reacted too slowly, and then he shifted towards Xiangcheng in the hope of joining hands with Xuangan's main body. News travelled very fast; the tidings of Xuangan's ruin at Dongdu reached the rebels first, and the host promptly came apart. The Sui deployment, by contrast, was layered. Da Xie Shanyi based five thousand picked troops at Hanyang Temple to meet Yang Jishan, who came in by way of Yanshi along the south bank of the Luo. Pei Hongce drew up eight thousand men at the White Sima Ford against Yang Xuanting, who crossed Mangshan to the south of the same ford; five engagements were fought in a single day, the Sui falling back, collecting their stragglers, reforming and fighting again. Wei Wensheng marched out of Huayin through the passes of Xiao and Mian, fighting as he marched and pressing straight for the city from the north, camping at Jingu and then on the sunny side of Mangshan, where he grappled with Xuangan in more than a dozen separate actions a day, wearing the enemy down by the rhythm of contact until Yang Xuanting was killed by an arrow and Xuangan's host gave ground a little. On the reinforcement side Qu Tutong first held Heyang and only crossed the river and took up at Poling after Fan Zigan had repeatedly struck at his camp and Xuangan had split his force; Lai Hu'er broke off the eastern naval operation and marched back from Donglai, while Yuwen Shu and the rest pursued by express post from Zhuojun. Xuangan finally abandoned the siege of the capital, proclaimed that he had taken the Eastern Capital and the passes beyond, and marched west for Tong Pass. At Huangtian Plain he deployed in a line fifty li deep, fighting as he marched, and was beaten three times in a single day; the collapse came at Dongdu Plain, and he turned on foot towards Jialu Garrison. On the technical side of siegecraft, the Sui had a fish-beam causeway and eight-wheeled tower carts ready at Liaodong, yet at the second watch of the night they cast everything away and marched back to the rescue. That was the decisive strategic turn of the whole campaign: the defenders of the capital received fresh troops, while the insurgents lost time.
data: 可以核對的數字集中在兩處。起義方面，韓相國在旬月之間聚眾十餘萬，旬月是十日到一月之間的時間單位，說明這支隊伍靠爆發式徵集而非長期整備，並在襄城一帶攻剽郡縣，最後潰散被擒。楊玄感主力可見的起點是五千餘名運夫少壯與三千餘名丹楊、宣城篙梢，渡河後眾益盛至十萬，屯上春門時日以千數有人請自效；東都一線則是達奚善意精兵五千、裴弘策八千、衛文升所率步騎二萬，與玄感在邙山之陽一日十餘合後死傷太半。攻城裝備方面，遼東前線造布囊百餘萬口盛土築魚梁大道，闊三十步、高與城齊，另有八輪樓車高出城牆，夜撤時軍資器械攻具積如丘山，全部棄置。處置數字見於事後推究：御史大夫裴蘊等奉命清算玄感黨與，所殺三萬餘人、籍沒其家，枉死者太半，流徙者六千餘人，另有韋福嗣、胡師耽等掌文書者被追究，虞綽、王冑逃亡被誅。距離上，襄城在洛陽西南，距東都約百餘公里，起義軍正是沿這條由梁郡通向襄城的通道作戰。
dataEn: The figures that can be checked cluster in two places. On the insurgent side, Han Xianguo drew more than a hundred thousand men within a few tens of days; a xun-yue is a span of between ten days and a month, and the phrase shows a force assembled by explosive levy rather than by long preparation, raiding the county seats around Xiangcheng before it finally broke up and was taken. The visible beginning of Yang Xuangan's main force was five thousand odd able-bodied carriers of grain and more than three thousand boatmen from Danyang and Xuancheng; after the crossing his host grew to a hundred thousand, and while he lay at Shangchun Gate men offered themselves to serve at the rate of a thousand a day. On the capital side there were five thousand picked troops under Da Xie Shanyi, eight thousand under Pei Hongce, and twenty thousand foot and horse under Wei Wensheng, whose losses were more than half after a dozen or more engagements on the sunny side of Mangshan in a single day. On siege equipment: at the Liaodong front more than a million cloth sacks were filled with earth to raise a fish-beam causeway thirty paces wide and as high as the wall, together with eight-wheeled tower carts that stood above the ramparts, and when the army withdrew in the night the military stores, weapons and siege tools lay piled like a hill and were all abandoned. The numbers of reprisal come from the subsequent investigation: the Censor-in-Chief Pei Yun and his colleagues were ordered to sift out the followers of Xuangan; more than thirty thousand were killed and their families confiscated, the greater part of those killed being innocent, and more than six thousand were exiled; men of the secretarial staff such as Wei Fusu and Hu Shidan were called to account, and Yu Chuo and Wang Zhou, who fled, were put to death. As for distance, Xiangcheng lies south-west of Luoyang, a little over a hundred kilometres from the Eastern Capital, and it was along this road from Liang Commandery towards Xiangcheng that the insurgents fought.
cause: 大業九年的一連串打擊是起義的直接背景。隋煬帝自大業八年冬再征高句麗，天下兵丁與糧秣大量北調，河南山東的丁壯大量被徵，遠征者的死亡比例在民間被記作「往歲天下全盛，吾輩父兄征高麗者猶太半不返」，役繁而無止境，郡縣官吏又趁機催斂。楊玄感是其中最有條件起來反擊的人：他是禮部尚書，出身關西勛戚，兄弟分任虎賁郎將與鷹揚郎將，掌握黎陽漕運，得以在督運時逗遲發船，令渡遼諸軍乏食；他又用家奴偽作使者，詐稱右驍衛大將軍來護兒已反，然後以討來護兒為名於六月乙巳入黎陽，閉城大索男夫，取帆布為牟甲，署官屬皆准開皇之舊，移書傍郡各令發兵會於倉所，郡縣有幹用者皆以運糧追集。七月玄感移兵東都，打出「廢昏立明」的書信，各地郡縣響應，河南的鄉里部曲在一夜之間被捲入。韓相國之舉，正是這股洪流的北段：隋廷在河南只留少量郡兵與京師宿衛，主力遠在涿郡與遼東，又正逢楊玄感起兵，洛陽與梁郡之間一時空了，於是平民韓相國舉兵響應，旬月聚眾十餘萬。
causeEn: The chain of blows that opened in the ninth year of Daye is the immediate background to the rising. The Sui Yangdi had set out to invade Goguryeo again in the winter of the eighth year of Daye; soldiers and grain from every province were moved north in bulk, the able-bodied men of Henan and Shandong were called up in numbers, and the rate of death among the men sent east was remembered in the villages as 'in the days when all under heaven was still flourishing, more than half of our fathers and elder brothers who went against Goguryeo never came back'. The corvées went on without end, while the officials of the counties took the opportunity to press the levies. Yang Xuangan was the man best placed to strike back. He was Minister of Rites, born of a powerful western family, his brothers held the rank of Colonel of the Household Guard and Eagle-Raising Colonel, and he controlled the grain transport at Liyang, which allowed him to hold up the sailing of the convoys and leave the armies crossing into Liaodong short of food. He had a servant of the household disguised as an envoy to spread the false report that Lai Hu'er, Right General of the Valiant Guards, had rebelled; and then, under the pretext of marching to punish Lai Hu'er, he entered Liyang on the yi-si day of the sixth month, closed the city, seized every man in it, took sailcloth for a felt cap and armour, and set up officials as in the Kaihuang era, sending letters to the neighbouring commanderies ordering each to send its fighting men to the granary. In the seventh month he moved his army against the Eastern Capital and dispatched a letter calling for the deposition of the darkened ruler and the elevation of the enlightened one; the counties answered, and the village levies of Henan were drawn in overnight. Han Xianguo's rising was the northern segment of that flood. The Sui court kept only a thin force of county troops and the capital's household guard in Henan, the bulk of its army lay far away at Zhuojun and in Liaodong, and with Xuangan's revolt in the middle of it the space between Luoyang and Liang Commandery stood momentarily empty; so a commoner named Han Xianguo took up arms, and within a few tens of days a hundred thousand men stood with him.
impact: 韓相國起義本身不足一年即告結束，留下的卻是隋末全局崩壞的第一塊骨牌。河南是隋朝漕運與丁役的取源地，一個梁郡平民能在旬月之內聚起十餘萬眾，說明鄉里社會已不再接受朝廷的調度，任何一個有號召力的人都能在空虛的郡縣迅速成軍。事後的清算更把這件事推向另一個方向：樊子蓋性既殘酷，裴蘊復奉旨峻法，所殺黨羽三萬餘人，皆籍沒其家，枉死者太半，流徙者六千餘人，這樣的高壓不但沒有止亂，反而把更多本可安居的人推向山東、江淮與南方。隋廷的注意力與兵力被一次次拉走，遼東攻具全部棄置，第二次征高句麗半途而廢，隋朝在中原的統治從此只剩下會打仗卻守不住州縣的樣子。與此同時，河南、江淮、山東、嶺南的起義互相援引，劉元進、朱燮與管崇、孟海公、格謙、白瑜娑等在同一年內先後起兵，隋末農民戰爭由此鋪開，唐朝的州縣與兵源也在這些起義隊伍的消耗中重組。韓相國的例子還留下一條後世反覆出現的教訓：起義隊伍可以靠十餘萬人的數量迅速膨脹，卻沒有後方、沒有補給線，一紙敗訊就能讓它散盡。
impactEn: Han Xianguo's rising itself lasted less than a year, yet it dropped the first domino of the general collapse of the late Sui. Henan was the province from which the Sui drew its river transport and its labour levies; the fact that a commoner of Liang Commandery could raise more than a hundred thousand men within a few tens of days shows that the village society had ceased to obey the court's calls, and that any man with a reputation could turn a hollow county into an army in a matter of days. The reckoning that followed pushed the matter in a worse direction: Fan Zigan was harsh by nature and Pei Yun carried out the court's order to apply the law without mercy, more than thirty thousand of the followers were killed and their families confiscated, the greater part of those killed being innocent, and more than six thousand were exiled. Far from ending the disorder, this pressure drove people who might otherwise have stayed where they were toward Shandong, Jianghuai and the south. Sui attention and manpower were pulled away again and again; the siege equipment at Liaodong was thrown away; the second Goguryeo campaign was abandoned halfway; and from then on the Sui held the central plain with nothing but the ability to fight battles and no ability to keep the prefectures. At the same time the risings in Henan, Jianghuai, Shandong and Lingnan invoked one another, and Liu Yuanjin, Zhu Xie with Guan Chong, Meng Haigong, Ge Qian and Bai Yusha all took up arms within the same year, so that the peasant war of the late Sui unfolded. Han Xianguo's case also left behind a lesson that recurs in later Chinese history: an insurgent host may swell to a hundred thousand men almost overnight, yet with no rear area and no supply line a single report of defeat can scatter it entirely.
result: 結局是失敗，而且失敗得很快。八月，隋軍在董杜原擊潰楊玄感主力：玄感布陳於董杜原，宇文述、衛文升、來護兒、屈突通諸軍合擊，大敗，玄感僅與十餘騎奔上洛，至葭蘆戍與弟積善徒步步行，自度不免，謂積善曰「我不能受人戮辱，汝可殺我」。消息傳到襄城一線時，韓相國的十餘萬眾「稍散」，沒有縱深、沒有糧秣的隊伍在失去主心骨後迅速瓦解，韓相國本人被隋朝官吏擒獲，傳首東都。首級送抵洛陽後，這場起義在史書上只剩下一段話的篇幅，留下姓名、兵眾數字與失敗原因。隋廷隨即在全國範圍內清剿各路起義，河南一線的劉元進、朱燮與管崇等部相繼被平定，但隋朝已無力恢復對河南的控制，大業十年的天下大亂與其後的王朝更替，都在這一年的失敗之後加速。
resultEn: The outcome was defeat, and a quick one. In the eighth month the Sui armies broke Yang Xuangan's main force at Dongdu Plain: Xuangan deployed at Dongdu, and the columns of Yuwen Shu, Wei Wensheng, Lai Hu'er and Qu Tutong closed in from every side and destroyed him. He fled with a dozen riders to Shangluo, and at Jialu Garrison he went on foot with his brother Jishan; reckoning that he could not escape, he told Jishan, 'I cannot bear to be taken and put to death; you had better kill me.' When the news reached the line at Xiangcheng, the hundred thousand odd men of Han Xianguo 'came apart a little': a host with no depth and no grain dissolved as soon as it lost its head, and Han Xianguo himself was taken by Sui officials and his head was carried to the Eastern Capital. Once the head reached Luoyang, this rising occupied no more than a sentence or two in the histories, leaving behind a name, a number of men and a reason for failure. The court then swept the country against the other risings, and in Henan the columns of Liu Yuanjin, Zhu Xie and Guan Chong were put down in turn; but the Sui no longer had the strength to recover Henan, and the great disorder of the land in the tenth year of Daye and the dynastic change that followed were both accelerated by this defeat of 613.
